title: The Last Great American Novel
gist: Ed Simon argues Franzen's The Corrections (2001) is the last book that could be recognized as a 'Great American Novel', not because great novels stopped being written but because the middlebrow culture and intellectual monoculture that could anoint one have collapsed. He reads the novel as anticipating the 2008 crash, bot farms and internet ubiquity, and calls Franzen's tech warnings prophetic in the AI era.

insights.claim: The Great American Novel can no longer be written because middlebrow culture has died; only lowbrow and an ever-shrinking highbrow remain.
insights.speaker: Hedgehog Review
insights.so_what: Fragmented attention markets erode mass-market cultural products and the gatekeepers who certify them.
